title: Flight booking lifecycle
idea: A flight booking's lifecycle is a state machine: it starts HELD and may only move along allowed arrows to CONFIRMED, TICKETED, EXPIRED or CANCELLED.
points: HELD moves to CONFIRMED on payment, EXPIRED on timeout, or CANCELLED.
CONFIRMED means paid; it becomes TICKETED once every passenger has a ticket.
EXPIRED and CANCELLED are final; their seats return to the fare count.
Ticketing is a separate step, so a paid booking survives a ticketing failure.

messages.label: hold(AI-101, Y-SAVER, 2 pax)
messages.note: The traveller picks a flight, a fare class and the passenger count.

messages.label: reserve(2)
messages.note: Two seats leave the fare count. The booking is created HELD.

messages.label: PNR-1, pay by 09:15
messages.note: The traveller gets a PNR and a deadline to show as a countdown.

messages.label: pay(PNR-1)
messages.note: Payment starts. The service first checks the hold is still HELD and in time.

messages.label: charge(900000)
messages.note: The gateway charges the total frozen at hold time.

messages.label: captured
messages.note: Money is taken, so the booking moves HELD to CONFIRMED.

messages.label: issue(PNR-1)
messages.note: Ticket numbers are created per passenger. This step can fail and be retried.

messages.label: TK-1, TK-2
messages.note: All passengers have tickets, so CONFIRMED moves to TICKETED.

messages.label: PNR-1 TICKETED
messages.note: Had the deadline passed first, the booking would be EXPIRED and the charge refused.

code.title: Status enum with rules
code.caption: The allowed moves live in the enum. Booking asks the enum before every change and keeps a history.

walk.text: PNR-1 takes the happy path, then the traveller cancels.
PNR-2 tries to skip payment, then expires, then gets a late payment.
An `EnumMap` lists the allowed next states for each state.
`canMoveTo` is the single question every transition asks.
Refuse and report an illegal move; otherwise change status and record it.

pitfalls: Do not set `status` from controllers; every change goes through `moveTo`.
A payment that lands after EXPIRED needs a refund, not a quiet confirm.
Do not jump HELD to TICKETED; issuing tickets for unpaid bookings loses money.

quiz.q: What is the first line PnrLifecycle prints for PNR-2?
quiz.why: HELD allows only CONFIRMED, EXPIRED and CANCELLED. TICKETED is not in that set, so `moveTo` prints the refusal and leaves status HELD.

takeaway: Write the allowed transitions once, in the enum, and refuse everything else.

starters: Why keep CONFIRMED and TICKETED as separate states?
What happens to a booking when the airline cancels the flight?
Should cancellation of a TICKETED booking depend on the fare class?
